description: INFOGRAPHIC CAPTURE only keeps the LAST match, and silently differs from the prior pipeline. stage1 line 14 assigns INFOG_REF[0]=... on every regex hit, so if an article references more than one 'images/<IMG_DIR>/what-is-*.png', only the final one is captured into manifest['infographic']; every earlier @@INFOG@@ marker is emitted in the body but stage2 has only ONE infographic path. stage2 line 36 does nb.replace('@@INFOG@@', ...) which is replace-ALL — so MULTIPLE @@INFOG@@ markers all collapse to the SAME single image, duplicating one infographic and dropping the others. The Automaton default happens to have exactly one what-is ref (line 26 of the md), so INV-1's count-only assertion (title/tables/mermaids, lines 109-111 of the test) cannot catch this; the spec GOAL 'reproduces current behavior byte-for-byte' is therefore unverified for the infographic, and a multi-infographic article regresses.
fix: Capture a LIST of infographic paths and emit indexed markers (@@INFOG1@@, @@INFOG2@@, ...) like tables/figs do; manifest['infographic'] becomes a list; stage2 iterates and replaces each indexed marker with its own uploaded image. Add a test fixture with two what-is-*.png refs asserting two distinct uploads. If single-infographic is an intentional invariant, assert in stage1 that at most one is matched and fail loudly otherwise.
